- When sentiment is consistently negative over recent days, model tends to over-forecast (especially after spikes), apply downward correction.
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots and fails to correct quickly — reduce forecast peak by 5–15% in next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment flips from negative to positive mid-period, model may lag in adjusting downward — apply early mean reversion bias.
- Model underestimates true volatility when sentiment is mixed or neutral — increase forecast variance or add 2–3% upward buffer for volatile periods.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 75), model tends to over-forecast — apply downward bias of 3–8% for next 5–7 days.
- When sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model often misaligns with sentiment direction — adjust forecast to match sentiment trend, not just price history.
